THESE APPEALS COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING THIS DAY, K.S.MUDAGAL J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Challenging the award in MVC No.3442/2020 passed by the I Addl. Small Causes Judge and MACT,
Bengaluru (SCCH 11), the claimants have preferred MFA No.6870/2022 and the Insurer has preferred MFA No.7176/2022.

sentences.text: For the purpose of convenience, the parties will be referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the trial Court.
Claimant No.1 is the wife, claimant No.2 is the daughter and claimants No.3 and 4 are the parents of the deceased Hadlee Francis.

3. On 06.12.2019 at about 8.30 a.m. when Hadlee Francis was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing Registration No.KA 03 JV 6508 near Vishnu Upahara Hotel on Old Chandapura village, the car bearing Registration No.KA 11 B 1274 hit the motor cycle of Hadlee Francis.

In the accident,
Hadlee Francis suffered fracture of left femur shaft.
Due to the injuries suffered in the accident Hadlee Francis was admitted in Best Hospital, Hosur Main road, Chandapura.
When he was in the hospital, Station House Officer, Suryanagar Police Station visited the hospital and recorded the statement of the victim as per Ex.P2.
Based on the said report, he registered FIR as per Ex.P1 against the driver of the car bearing No.KA 11 B 1274 in Crime No.396/2019 of their police station.

On investigation, the Police filed charge sheet on 03.10.2020 as per Ex.P15 against respondent No.1.
4.

In Best Hospital the victim underwent surgery for his fractured left femur and he was discharged from the hospital on 09.12.2019 which is evident from Ex.P30 the discharge summary of the Best Hospital.
Subsequently on 25.12.2019 as some complications developed, he was taken to Best Hospital where he was declared as 'brought dead'.

On 27.12.2019 PW.3 Assistant Professor,
Department of Forensic Medicine, Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru conducted post mortem examination.
He issued Post mortem report Ex.P10 on 14.09.2020 stating that the death is consequent upon the injuries sustained.

Thereafter on 03.10.2020 the Investigating Officer filed charge sheet as per Ex.P15 against the driver of the car for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC alleging that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the car bearing No.KA 11 B 1274 by respondent No.1 and Hadlee Francis died due to the injuries suffered in the accident.

sentences.text: At the relevant time, respondent Nos.1 and 2 were the registered owner and Insurer of the car bearing No.KA 11 B 1274.

The claimants filed MVC No.3442/2020 against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.2 crores on the ground that the accident and consequential death occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the car by the first respondent.
They claimed that they were dependent on the income of the deceased.
Therefore, the respondents are liable to compensate damages caused to them.
6. Respondent No.1 did not contest the petition.

Respondent No.2 alone contested the petition denying rashness and negligence on the part of the first respondent, the injuries suffered by the victim, nexus between the death and the injuries suffered by him, his age, occupation and income and its liability to pay the compensation.
7. To substantiate their case, the claimants examined PWs.1 to 4 on their behalf and got marked Ex.P1 to P37.

Respondent No.2 examined their panel doctor as RW.1 and their official as RW.2 and got marked Exs.R.1 and R.2.
8.

The Tribunal on hearing both side by the impugned order relying on Exs.P1 to P15 and the evidence of PW.3 held that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the first respondent.
The Tribunal further held that the death of Hadlee Francis was on account of the injuries suffered in the accident.
9. The Tribunal relying on Ex.P19 considered the age of the deceased as 33 years.

Relying on the evidence of PW.4 and Exhs.P31 to 36 assessed his annual income at Rs.6,88,021/- added 50% of the same by way of future prospects, deducted one-fourth from the same for his personal expenses and awarded compensation of Rs.1,23,84,384/- on the head of loss of dependency.

10. The Tribunal in all awarded Rs.1,25,74,384/- on different heads as per the table below:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency and 1,23,84,384/-
 loss of future income

2 . Loss Of Consortium 40,000/-
 Parental Consortium 40,000/-
 Filial consortium of children 80,000/-
 (40,000 X 2)
 3. Loss of estate & funeral 30,000/-
 expenses

Total Compensation 1,25,74,384/-
11.

sentences.text: Accident occurred on 06.12.2019 and the death occurred on 25.12.2019.
As per the medical records, Ex.P30 produced by the claimants themselves show that the claimant had surgery and his condition was stable.
The only injury suffered by him was fracture of left femur and the claimants absolutely did not adduce any evidence to connect the nexus between death and accidental injuries.
PW.3 was only a doctor who conducted Post-mortem Examination.
Even Post-mortem Examination report does not show any septicimic injuries or thrombosis or any hemorrhage.
If at all the cause of death is proximate to death, the best witnesses to speak about that are the doctors who treated the deceased in the hospital.
The Tribunal committed error in holding that the death was on account of the injuries suffered in the accident.

When the claimants were not able to establish the nexus between the death and the accidental injuries, the question of awarding compensation on the head of loss of dependency, consortium etc does not arise.
The future prospects awarded at the rate of 50% is untenable.
Submissions of Smt.Mamatha D.N., learned counsel for 13.
PW.3 is the best person to speak about the cause of death.
Even if the treating doctors at Best Hospital were examined, they would not have spoken about the cause of death as they had not conducted the post-mortem examination.
Therefore, the Tribunal was justified in relying on the evidence of PW.3 regarding cause of death.
The notional income assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Consequently the compensation awarded on the head of loss of dependency is on the lower side.

Having regard to the submissions of both side, the questions that arise for determination of the Court are:
i) Whether the trial court was justified in holding that the death of Hadlee Francis was on account of the injuries suffered by him on 06.12.2019 in the accident.?
ii) Whether the compensation awarded is just one ?
Analysis 15.
The deceased was the victim of the accident.

Soon after the accident, on receiving information,
the Station House Officer, Suryanagar Police station recorded the statement of the deceased as per Ex.P2.
Since the victim died before the claim petition was filed, the same is admissible in evidence in view of Section 32 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
In the said complaint, he has imputed the negligence to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 did not dispute the said fact either by filing written statement or by entering the witness box.
Therefore, the Tribunal was justified in holding that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence of respondent No.1. Reg: Cause of death.
16. Admittedly, the accident occurred on 06.12.2019.

PW.2, who is the public relations Officer of Best hospital,

sentences.text: The said documents show that Hadlee Francis was admitted into the Hospital on 06.12.2019 with the history of RTA and had sustained injury over left thigh and left knee abrasion.
On investigation, as per Ex.P30 it was found that he had suffered fracture of left femur.
He underwent surgery for left femur nailing on 06.12.2019 and he was discharged from the hospital on 09.12.2019.
P30 states that at the time of discharge, the patient was stable and had no other complications.

The evidence on record and the award of the Tribunal show that an attempt was made by the claimants to contend that the victim died due to the complications arising out of the surgeries conducted for accidental injuries.
Further an attempt was made to elicit that when such surgeries are conducted there is likelihood of blood clotting due to cutting of the vessels leading to hemorrhage etc.

Though PW.3-doctor claimant's own witness gives the final opinion that death is consequent upon the injuries suffered in the accident, he does not say what were the complications developed after the surgery.
There is no - 12 - whisper in his chief examination about any septicemia, thrombosis or hemorrhage suffered by the victim.
18. It is material to note that when the victim became indisposable, the claimants had taken him again to Best Hospital only, where he was declared 'brought dead'.
At this stage, some doctors in the Best Hospital must have examined him.

Two doctors who conducted the surgery in the Best Hospital or treated him would be the best persons to speak about what kind of complications are likely to arise and whether such complications are fatal and they may lead to death.
Absolutely no reasons were assigned for suppressing such material evidence.
19. The injuries mentioned in Ex.P10 are external injuries.
In the FSL report the residues of volatile poisons, Pesticides, Barbiturates, Benzodiazepine, group of drugs, toxic metals, ions and anions were not detected.

The histopathology report extracted in Ex.P10 is to the effect that there was coronary artery disease with left circumflex artery and anterior descending artery showing athesoscleions with non-critical narrowing of lumen.
Whether those kinds of complications - 13 - could arise because of the accidental injuries suffered by the victim could have been spoken by the doctor who treated him.
Under such circumstances, the Tribunal was not justified in relying only on the evidence of PW.3 to come to the conclusion that the death was proximate to accidental injuries of the victim.
However, the claimants should not be driven out of the Court on such lapses as they have lost their breadwinner.

sentences.text:
In the judgment in United India Insurance Company vs.
M.Elangoven2, the victim had suffered temporal bone fracture which had led to systemic sepsis,
multi-organ dysfunction, septic shock and cardiopulmonary arrest. Therefore, the judgments relied on by learned Counsel for the claimants cannot be justifiably applied to the facts of the present case.

sentences.text: Under the circumstances, it is a fit case to remand the matter to the Tribunal to afford an opportunity to the claimants to examine the doctors of Best Hospital who treated Hadlee Francis between 06.12.2019 and 09.12.2019 and attended the deceased on 25.12.2019.
When the nexus between the death and injury itself was not conclusively proved, the question of considering whether the quantum of compensation was just or not does not arise.

Hence the following:
ORDER i) The appeals are partly allowed.
ii) The impugned award is hereby set aside.
iii) The matter is remanded to the Tribunal for fresh consideration on recording medical evidence referred to in the body of this judgment.
iv) To avoid further delay, the parties shall appear before the Tribunal on 10.04.2023 without any further notice.
v) The Tribunal shall record the evidence and dispose of the matter within three months from the date fixed for such appearance of the parties.
- 15 - Registry shall refund the amount in deposit to the Insurer and transmit the records to the Tribunal forthwith.
